weight.what: Your total body weight: muscle, fat, bone, water, everything.
weight.why: Weight alone can't tell fat from muscle. Read it together with your muscle and body fat.
weight.tip: Aim for slow, steady change rather than quick drops. Your coach can help you set a target.

muscle.what: Skeletal muscle: the muscle you train and move with.
muscle.why: More muscle makes you stronger, protects your joints, and burns more calories even at rest.
muscle.tip: Lift weights regularly and eat enough protein. Going up is good news.

bodyFat.what: How much of your weight is fat, as a percentage.
bodyFat.why: It shows your fitness better than weight does, because it separates fat from muscle.
bodyFat.tip: Train regularly, sleep well, and eat a little less than you burn. Going down is good news.

water.what: All the water in your body: in your muscles, blood, and organs.
water.why: Staying hydrated keeps your energy up and helps you train and recover.
water.tip: Drink water through the day, and more on training days.

protein.what: The protein in your body, mostly in your muscles.
protein.why: It shows whether your body has what it needs to build and keep muscle.
protein.tip: Have some protein with every meal: chicken, eggs, fish, beans, or dairy.

minerals.what: The minerals in your body, mostly in your bones.
minerals.tip: Eat a varied diet with dairy and leafy greens. Strength training helps your bones too.

bmr.what: The calories your body burns in a day just to keep running, before any exercise.
bmr.why: It is the starting point for how much you can eat each day.
bmr.tip: Building muscle raises it a little, so strength training helps.

bmi.what: Your weight compared with your height.
bmi.why: A quick general check: 18.5–25 is the usual healthy range. It can't tell muscle from fat, so very muscular people can read high.
bmi.tip: Read it next to your body fat and muscle, not on its own.

visceral.what: Fat stored deep in your belly, around your organs.
visceral.why: A high level is linked to health risks, even in people who look slim.
visceral.tip: Lower is better. Regular exercise, good sleep, and less sugar help bring it down.

leanGain.title: Building muscle
leanGain.body: You added {{muscle}} of muscle and your fat stayed about the same.
leanGain.next: Keep lifting heavy and eat enough protein so the muscle keeps coming.

fatLoss.title: Losing fat
fatLoss.body: You lost {{fat}} of fat and kept your muscle.
fatLoss.next: Keep strength training so the weight you lose stays fat, not muscle.

bulk.title: Gaining size
bulk.body: You added {{muscle}} of muscle and {{fat}} of fat.
bulk.next: Want less fat with the muscle? Cut the extra snacks and keep training.

cutting.title: Losing weight
cutting.body: You lost {{fat}} of fat, but also {{muscle}} of muscle.
cutting.next: Add protein and keep lifting so you only lose fat.

fatGain.title: Fat went up
fatGain.body: Your fat went up {{fat}} and your muscle didn't grow.
fatGain.next: Talk to your coach about your meals and add some cardio.

muscleLoss.title: Muscle dipped
muscleLoss.body: You lost {{muscle}} of muscle while your fat stayed about the same.
muscleLoss.next: Train each muscle group twice a week and eat protein at every meal.

steady.title: Holding steady
steady.body: Your muscle and fat barely changed.
steady.next: Ready for more? Ask your coach for a new goal.

fitScoreInfo.title: What is FitScore?
fitScoreInfo.what: A number from 0 to 100. It compares your muscle and body fat with a healthy standard for your body. Higher is better.
fitScoreInfo.tip: Lift weights about 3 times a week and eat enough protein. More muscle and less fat both raise your score.
